claim.pdf_says: UNLOCK file-name-1 [ RECORD | RECORDS ]  (one line: UNLOCK, then file-name-1, then a bracket stacking RECORD over RECORDS)
claim.why_it_matters: A reader or grammar author working from the transcription could take file-name-1 for an alternative stacked with UNLOCK, or misorder it relative to the optional RECORD/RECORDS bracket, and so derive the wrong UNLOCK syntax.
claim.detail: In the drawn figure, file-name-1 sits on a different row, in the same column as UNLOCK and below it, rather than after UNLOCK on the baseline. Read as a diagram, UNLOCK and file-name-1 look stacked in one column, and their order relative to the bracket is unclear. The printed format is UNLOCK file-name-1 followed by an optional bracket (no choice bars) holding RECORD/RECORDS. Suggested fix: put 'UNLOCK file-name-1' on the middle row before the bracket.

verdict.reasoning: The 300 dpi render of PDF page 566 (printed page 544), §2002:14.8.43.1, shows UNLOCK (underlined) and file-name-1 on one baseline, followed by a plain bracket with no choice bars that stacks RECORD over RECORDS. The bracket means at most one of them, and it is optional. page-566.md lines 10-13 put UNLOCK on row 1 and file-name-1 on row 3, both starting at column 0, so the two are vertically stacked to the left of the bracket. In this notation, vertically stacked items read as alternatives, so the transcription suggests UNLOCK and file-name-1 are alternatives, which changes the syntax. The bracket itself is transcribed correctly: plain, with RECORD/RECORDS. The claim quotes both sources accurately.
